group.title: Fruit and vegetables
group.tagline: Fresh food to buy and eat
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A round, sweet fruit with a thick skin, the color of a carrot.
examples: I drink {orange} juice in the morning.
wrong: I wear an orange on my head to keep warm.

words.meaning: A small round green or purple fruit.
wrong: A grape is as big as a car.

words.meaning: A small, soft, red fruit with seeds on the outside.
wrong: A strawberry is a blue vegetable.

words.meaning: A yellow fruit with a sour taste.
wrong: The lemon is very sweet and purple.

words.meaning: A sweet green or yellow fruit, wide at the bottom.
wrong: A pear is a fruit I drink milk from.

words.meaning: A soft round fruit with a fuzzy skin and a big stone.
wrong: The peach is hard like a rock.

words.meaning: A small round red fruit with a stone inside.
examples: There’s a {cherry} on top of the cake.
wrong: A cherry is as big as a watermelon.

words.meaning: A big fruit with a hard skin and sweet yellow inside.
wrong: A pineapple is a tree that grows apples.

words.meaning: A very big green fruit that is red and juicy inside.
examples: We ate {watermelon} in the hot sun.
wrong: The watermelon fits in my small pocket.

words.meaning: A big round fruit with a hard skin and soft inside.
wrong: A melon is a tiny seed.

words.meaning: A sweet fruit with yellow inside and a big stone.
wrong: A mango is a kind of fish.

words.meaning: A small, round, soft fruit, often purple.
examples: The {plums} on the tree are ready.
wrong: A plum is a vegetable as long as my arm.

words.meaning: A small green fruit with a sour taste.
wrong: The lime is big, red and sweet.

words.meaning: A big brown nut with white food and milk inside.
wrong: The coconut is soft like a grape.

words.meaning: A very small, round, dark blue fruit.
wrong: A blueberry is a big yellow fruit.

words.meaning: A small soft fruit with lots of seeds.
wrong: A berry is a big tree.

words.meaning: A small brown fruit that is green inside.
wrong: A kiwi is a big orange vegetable.

words.meaning: A green fruit with soft inside and a big stone.
wrong: An avocado is a sweet red berry.

words.meaning: A small green or black fruit used for oil.
wrong: An olive is as big as a melon.

words.meaning: A dry fruit with a hard shell.
wrong: A nut is soft and full of juice.

words.meaning: A small soft red fruit.
wrong: A raspberry is a green vegetable.

words.meaning: A small soft orange fruit with a stone.
wrong: An apricot is a big green leaf.

words.meaning: A long orange vegetable that grows in the ground.
wrong: A carrot is a blue fruit that grows on trees.

words.meaning: A big round vegetable with green leaves.
wrong: A cabbage is a small red berry.

words.meaning: A green vegetable with big leaves, eaten in salads.
wrong: We fry lettuce to make it a cake.

words.meaning: A long green vegetable that is cool and wet inside.
examples: I cut a {cucumber} for the salad.
wrong: A cucumber is a round orange fruit.

words.meaning: A seed or a long thin pod that you cook and eat.
wrong: A bean is as big as a watermelon.

words.meaning: A very small round green vegetable.
wrong: A pea is a long white vegetable.

words.meaning: A tall plant with yellow seeds that you eat.
wrong: Corn is a purple fruit with a stone.

words.meaning: A small plant shaped like an umbrella that you can eat.
wrong: A mushroom is a sweet orange fruit.

words.meaning: A small white plant with a strong taste, used in cooking.
examples: This sauce has a lot of {garlic}.
wrong: Garlic has no smell or taste at all.

words.meaning: A green vegetable that looks like a little tree.
examples: Eat your {broccoli}, it’s good for you.
wrong: Broccoli is a yellow fruit.

words.meaning: A vegetable with soft dark green leaves.
wrong: Spinach is a hard red fruit.

words.meaning: A big round orange vegetable.
wrong: A pumpkin is as small as a pea.

words.meaning: A vegetable with long light green stems.
wrong: Celery is a round purple fruit.

words.meaning: A vegetable with a big white head.
wrong: A cauliflower is a pink flower you give to people.

words.meaning: A root vegetable with orange inside that tastes a little sweet.
wrong: A sweet potato is a kind of candy.

words.meaning: A long vegetable with a shiny purple skin.
wrong: An eggplant is a bird that lays eggs.

words.meaning: A long green vegetable that looks like a cucumber.
wrong: A zucchini is a small red berry.

words.meaning: Ready to eat because it has grown fully.
wrong: The ripe banana is too green and hard to eat.
